I think it's going to be exceptionally unpredictable largely because of automation.

Tesla recently announced the plan to complete the first coast to coast completely autonomous roadtrip and have video available by next year. Full scale automation on a similar scale will follow by 2018. I think most people aren't really thinking about what this means. Taxis, commercial transport, local logistics - those are a huge number of jobs and still pay very well relative to the skill involved. They're going to be automated away imminently and will have a cascading effect on unemployment. Even the Fed is proactively researching their options in case of, as they call it, "idiosyncratic shocks to employment."

I think it's borderline impossible to try to predict in any sort of intelligent fashion what this will do to the labor force, how the government will respond, how private enterprise will respond, and so on - other than the impact will be very big. There's also constant general AI research which is still progressing exponentially. It's unclear whether we've entered into another sort of sigmoid curve (an initially exponential curve that levels out) or this rate of progress will continue. In the latter case, things there could have an even larger and again equally unpredictable impact. And that's really just scratching the surface of everything that's going on. As always I think the big picture is ultimately going to be shaped by the direction that science and technology takes us and it's going to be taking us to some very unknown places.
